sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
What multidimensional arrays are and why they’re useful
• How to create and use 2D arrays (like spreadsheets!)
• Real-world examples where they shine

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine a **chessboard**. It’s not just a list of squares - it’s a grid with rows and columns. That’s exactly what a 2D array is!

Think of it like:
- A **spreadsheet** (rows × columns)
- A **game board** (like tic-tac-toe)
- A **pixel grid** in an image

In Java, a 2D array is simply an array of arrays. Here’s the magic:

**Declaring a 2D array** is easy:
```java
int[][] grid = new int[3][3]; // 3 rows, 3 columns
```

• First `[]` = rows (like floors in a building)
• Second `[]` = columns (like rooms on each floor)
• You can have 3D, 4D... but 2D is most common!
sections.title: Core Concepts

sections.content:
**Accessing elements** works like coordinates:
```java
grid[1][2] = 5; // Row 1, Column 2 gets value 5
```

• Remember: **indexes start at 0** (like most arrays)
• `grid.length` = number of rows
• `grid[0].length` = number of columns in first row

Code Examples
Key Points
points: A multidimensional array is an array of arrays, extending data to two or more dimensions
A 2D array is declared as: dataType[][] name = new dataType[rows][columns]
2D arrays are useful for representing matrices, tables, grids, and game boards
Each row in a 2D array is itself a one-dimensional array
Multidimensional arrays can have more than two dimensions, though 2D is most common

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Multidimensional arrays organize data in grids (2D), cubes (3D), etc. Most important rule: `array[row][col]` for access. Practice with nested loops to process them efficiently.

questions.question: What is a two-dimensional array?
options: An array of arrays, organized in rows and columns
An array that can only hold two data types
questions.explanation: A two-dimensional array is an array of arrays, organized like a table with rows and columns. It can be used to represent matrices, grids, or tables of data.

questions.question: How do you access an element in a 2D array at row 2, column 3?
questions.explanation: In Java, 2D array elements are accessed using two indices: arr[row][column]. So arr[2][3] accesses row 2, column 3 (both zero-indexed).
